blind_spots.blind_spot: Platform is explicitly cloud-based SaaS with no offline/air-gapped mode described anywhere on the site.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Firmware/software living on classified or IL5 weapons-platform networks can't reach a public SaaS backend to run binary analysis — the exact DDIL failure mode the checklist flags.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product was built and sold for commercial enterprise supply-chain security first; the AFWERX contract is a bolt-on use case, not the design center.

blind_spots.operator_reality: A DoD program office doesn't 'compare products and drive remediation through procurement' — findings feed a POA&M under an Authority to Operate, with STIG and IL4/IL5 timelines the site never mentions.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Sales motion and case studies (XZ Utils, Log4j, SolarWinds, 3CX) are all commercial-breach narratives, not defense acquisition narratives.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention of how firmware binaries from classified/embedded weapons systems get into the platform for analysis without violating data-handling rules.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Embedded/firmware SBOM work for DoD platforms routinely involves ITAR-controlled binaries and export-restricted vendor code; uploading that to a commercial SaaS analysis pipeline is itself a compliance question the pack never addresses.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Own-language treats 'analyze third-party code without waiting' as a pure technical capability, with no export-control or data-sovereignty framing.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Analyze third-party code without waiting — Inspect purchased software and devices without relying on vendor self-attestations or delayed disclosures.
